title: 2011 Player Eval Techniques - NBA
universal_lens: A finite state machine models NBA gameplay as discrete states and transitions, enabling probabilistic inference over player contributions via action-based credit assignment. A four-state Markovian framework models basketball possessions as normal or extra for each team, enabling probabilistic transition dynamics.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs Bayesian inference to update player impact probabilities using observed state transitions and action outcomes within a conformal predictive framework. Bayesian belief updates on possession states inform player credit assignment via conformal predictive distributions over scoring events.
gse_mapping: GSE utilizes state-transition graphs to simulate real-time tactical decisions, mapping player actions to expected possession outcomes and strategic value adjustments. Situational reasoning engine encodes state transitions using deterministic automata with stochastic rewards for tactical decision-making.

primitives.name: Finite State Game Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: This approach models a basketball game as a finite state machine, which is a behavior model composed of a finite number of states, transitions between those states, and actions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S': 'set of game states', 'T': 'set of state transitions', 'A': 'set of player actions'}
primitives.assumptions: Gameplay is modeled as a Markov process with discrete time steps and deterministic state transitions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When state transitions become stochastic or non-Markovian due to external factors.

layer2.mapping: The finite state machine maps directly to GSE's decision tree nodes where each node represents a game state and edges represent actions leading to next states.
layer2.telemetry: Transition frequency matrices derived from play-by-play data.

primitives.name: Four Team State Machine
primitives.verbatim_quote: This state machine consists of four states, a 'normal' and an 'extra possession'-state for each of the two teams.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_n': 'normal state for team n', 'S_e': 'extra possession state for team n'}
primitives.assumptions: Each team has exactly two distinct states: normal possession and extra possession.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When possession does not result in clear transition to either normal or extra state.

layer2.mapping: Derived from the base finite state model; represents a partitioned subset of states specific to team-specific dynamics.
layer2.telemetry: Proportion of possessions ending in extra state per team.

primitives.name: Turnover/Rebound Trigger Mechanism
primitives.verbatim_quote: The 'extra possession'-state can be reached through forcing opponent turnovers or offensive rebounds.
primitives.assumptions: Turnovers and offensive rebounds are independent events that trigger state change.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When event probability distribution shifts beyond baseline expectations.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's event-triggered state update mechanism where specific actions (e.g., steal, rebound) cause immediate state transition.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of turnover/rebound events triggering extra possession state.

primitives.name: Player Credit Assignment
primitives.verbatim_quote: Players get positive and negative credit assigned to them for executing certain actions or failure to do so.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C_p': 'credit assigned to player p', 'A_i': 'action i performed by player p'}
primitives.assumptions: Credit assignment is linearly dependent on action execution quality and outcome.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When individual player influence becomes indistinguishable from collective team effect.

layer2.mapping: Derived from state transition credit system; assigns scalar values to players based on contribution to state evolution.
layer2.telemetry: Mean deviation of predicted vs actual margin of victory when adjusting player credits.

primitives.name: Possession State Machine
primitives.verbatim_quote: 1 The States In the context of this method we define four different states for a basketball game, a 'normal' possession and an 'extra' possession for each of the two teams.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_n': 'Set of normal possession states for Team A and B', 'S_e': 'Set of extra possession states for Team A and B', 'T': 'Time index of possession event'}
primitives.assumptions: Each possession follows a Markov process; state transitions depend only on current state and action.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Transition probabilities become undefined when both teams are in extra state simultaneously.

layer2.mapping: State space is isomorphic to a discrete-time Markov chain with absorbing states representing end-of-possession outcomes.
layer2.telemetry: Observed possession outcome frequency per state transition.

primitives.name: Shot Outcome Classifier
primitives.verbatim_quote: In case of a shot at the basket a team can enter the 'extra' state through offensive rebounding.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_o': 'Offensive rebound indicator (0 or 1)', 'S_m': 'Shot made indicator (0 or 1)', 'D_r': 'Defensive rebound indicator (0 or 1)'}
primitives.assumptions: Shot outcomes are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive; rebounding affects subsequent possession state.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When R_o=1, team enters 'extra' state; otherwise, opponent enters 'normal' state.

layer2.mapping: Derived from possession state machine kernel; maps shot events to updated state vector.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of offensive vs defensive rebounding post-shot.

primitives.name: Turnover Trigger Mechanism
primitives.verbatim_quote: An additional way of entering a teams' 'extra' state is by forcing the opponent team into a turnover while it is currently in its 'normal' state.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T_f': 'Turnover forcing event (0 or 1)', 'S_{op}': "Opponent's current state (normal or extra)", 'S_{t}': "Team's new state after turnover"}
primitives.assumptions: Turnovers occur stochastically; forcing a turnover changes opponent’s state to normal unless already in extra.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If S_{op}=normal, then S_{t}=extra; else S_{t}=normal.

layer2.mapping: Turnover event triggers a conditional update in the state vector based on opponent's prior state.
layer2.telemetry: Rate of forced turnovers per possession type.
